To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the shock response of viscoelastically damped sandwich beams can be reduced significantly (up to 80 percent) compared with the undamped beams, the performance of two- and five-layer beams are comparable, the performance of three-layer beams are inferior, the damping effectiveness is not significantly affected by the shock duration, and the damping effectiveness increases with the shock intensity.

the shock response and the damping effectiveness of visoelastically damped two-, and three-layer simply supported sandwich structures are comparable and that five-layer simply supported viscoelastically damped sandwich structures are superior in shock response and damping.

the performance of a sandwich structure is not a function of its number of layers but depends on the thickness ratio and the relative stiffness of its layers, and that the optimum damping effectiveness is achieved when the faces are made of viscoelastic material.
In summary, our research is concerned with
(1) The effect of the viscoelastically damped multilayer structure on the shock response of the structure.

the development of a general method to analyze the response of viscoelastically damped multilayer structures subjected to shock excitation, and the application of this method to the design of sandwich beams for shock mitigation.

the following: (1) to develop a generalized theory for the shock response and the damping effectiveness of viscoleastically damped multilayer structures; and (2) to compare the relative performance of two-, three-, five-layer simply supported beams subjected to shock excitation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the three-layer sandwich beam is the most efficient one for shock response and damping.
the two-layer structure has the best performance for the given shock pulse shape and the five-layer structure is the best for the given weight and size constraints.
the five-layer structure is the best choice for shock mitigation, followed by the three-layer and two-layer structure, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the same damping and size-and-weight criteria, the three-layer sandwich beam is the most effective in reducing the shock response of the structure.

the two-layer sandwich structure has a better damping effectiveness for the shock response than the three-layer sandwich structure, and that the five-layer sandwich structure has an inferior performance compared to the other two sandwich structures.

the damping effectiveness of a viscoelastically damped multilayer structure subjected to shock excitation is not a simple function of the number of layers, and that the performance of a structure is not a simple linear function of its weight.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the five-layer configuration is superior to the two- and three-layer configurations for the same size and weight, in terms of shock response and damping.
, for a given weight and size, the three-layer structure is more effective than the other two in reducing the shock response.
for the same weight and size of the beam, the three- and five-layer sandwich beams have better damping effectiveness than the two-layer beam.
